{
  "root_cause": "The navigation controller adds a keydown listener on every start() call without removing previous listeners, causing duplicate listeners. On Enter, multiple listeners fire, and the final input value depends on the order of simulated clicks, leading to an incorrect selection (Blueberry instead of Blackberry).",
  "repair_strategy": "Ensure only one keydown listener is active at a time by storing the current listener on the input field and removing it before adding a new one.",
  "edits": [
    {
      "path": "src/controllers/navigationController.js",
      "sha256": "cb38337c041e8e0543c4f7b31666374956d6dc85011604e12ff127c9bf67ddde",
      "before": "  const navigate = config.resultsList.navigation || navigation;\n  /**\n   * @listens {keydown} Listens to all `keydown` events on the input field\n   **/\n  config.inputField.addEventListener(\"keydown\", navigate);",
      "after": "  const navigate = config.resultsList.navigation || navigation;\n  /**\n   * @listens {keydown} Listens to all `keydown` events on the input field\n   **/\n  // Remove previous listener if exists\n  if (config.inputField._navListener) {\n    config.inputField.removeEventListener(\"keydown\", config.inputField._navListener);\n  }\n  config.inputField.addEventListener(\"keydown\", navigate);\n  config.inputField._navListener = navigate;"
  }
],
"expected_accessibility_effect": "Keyboard navigation will correctly reflect the highlighted suggestion when Enter is pressed, preserving ARIA activedescendant and selection states, ensuring the form receives the intended value.",
"functional_risks": [
  "If the cleanup fails, keyboard navigation could break.",
  "The custom property _navListener must not conflict with other code.",
  "Assumes no other part of the system relies on multiple keydown listeners."
],
"verification_requirements": [
  "After typing 'bl', pressing ArrowDown twice then Enter, the input value should be 'Blackberry'.",
  "Arrow Up/Down navigation should correctly highlight and update aria-activedescendant.",
  "Escape key should clear the input and close the suggestion list.",
  "No duplicate keydown listeners should be present on the input field after multiple searches."
}
}

But then step 5: type "l", assertion: text of #autoComplete_result_0 equals "Blackberry".
So after typing "bl", the filtered list yields maybe: Blackberry, Blackcurrant, Blueberry? Actually starting letters "bl": Banana (starts Ba), Bilberry (Bi), Blackberry (Bl), Blackcurrant (Bl), Blueberry (Bl). So after typing "bl", suggestions: Blackberry, Blackcurrant, Blueberry. They assert that result_0 text is "Blackberry". Good.

Then step 6: press ArrowDown (third down?) Actually after typing l, they had already typed "b" then typed "l"? Wait timeline: Step2 type b -> suggestions open showing many. Then step3 ArrowDown (first down) maybe moves highlight to first result (Banana?). Step4 ArrowDown (second down) moves highlight to second result (Bilberry?). But they assert after step4 that aria-selected on #autoComplete_result_0 is true. That seems contradictory: after two downs, they expect result_0 selected? Unless the list is zero-indexed and they start at -1? Let's examine navigation logic.

In navigationController.js, they have currentFocus initialized -1. On keydown down (or tab) they call update(event, list, true, config). In update: if state true (down/tab) increment currentFocus, else decrement. Then they call addActive(list). addActive removes active from all, then if currentFocus >= list.length set to 0; if <0 set to list.length-1; then set aria-selected true on list[currentFocus].

Thus initial currentFocus = -1. First down: state true => currentFocus becomes 0. addActive: list[0] gets aria-selected true. So after first down, result_0 selected.

Second down: currentFocus becomes 1. addActive: list[1] selected.

Thus after two downs, result_1 selected, not result_0. However the test asserts after step4 (second down) that aria-selected on result_0 is true. Something off.

Maybe they consider that after typing "b", the list hasn't been rendered yet until after composition? Actually they type b, then assertion aria-expanded true (list open). Then they press ArrowDown (first down) - maybe they expect nothing because list not yet populated? But they have no assertions. Then second ArrowDown triggers selection of result_0 due to some logic? Let's look at observed failure: At step6 (Enter press) they expected form-data fruit = ["Blackberry"] but observed ["Blueberry"].

Let's reconstruct the state at step6 according to observed logs.

From observed "after" for step6 (Enter press): they show input html with aria-expanded false, aria-activedescendant missing (since after Enter they closed list). Before step6 (just before Enter) they show input html with aria-expanded true and aria-activedescendant="autoComplete_result_0". Now we need to see how navigation updates currentFocus across these events, considering that after typing l, the list may be re-rendered (filtered) which could reset currentFocus? Let's examine the code.

Thus on each input event (including after typing l), they close all lists, then start (which generates list and calls navigate). navigate adds keydown listener.

However note that navigate is called each time start is called (i.e., after each input). navigate adds another keydown listener each time? /**
 * List navigation function initializer
 *
 * @param {Object} config - autoComplete configurations
 * @param {Object} dataFeedback - The available data object
 *
 */
const navigate = (config, dataFeedback) => {
  // Reset focus state
  let currentFocus = -1;

  /**
   * Update list item state
   *
   * @param {Object} event - The `keydown` event Object
   * @param {Array <elements>} list - The array of list items
   * @param {Boolean} state - Of the arrow Down/Up
   * @param {Object} config - autoComplete configurations
   *
   */
  const update = (event, list, state, config) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    if (state) {
      // If the arrow DOWN or TAB key is pressed
      // increase the currentFocus
      currentFocus++;
    } else {
      // If the arrow UP or TAB key is pressed
      // decrease the currentFocus
      currentFocus--;
    }
    // and add "active" class to the list item
    addActive(list);
    config.inputField.setAttribute("aria-activedescendant", list[currentFocus].id);
    /**
     * @emits {navigation} Emits Event on results list navigation
     **/
    eventEmitter(
      event.srcElement,
      { event, ...dataFeedback, selection: dataFeedback.results[currentFocus] },
      "navigation"
    );
  };

  /**
   * Remove list item active state
   *
   * @param {Array <elements>} list - The array of list items
